name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
variant: Seated calf-raise machine with the knees flexed around 90 degrees and resistance applied through a thigh pad; treated separately from standing, donkey, leg-press, and bodyweight calf raises.
description: Sit with the balls of the feet on the platform, the knees bent and held under the thigh pad, and the ankles free to move. Lower the heels under control until the calves are stretched, press through the forefoot to raise the heels as high as controlled, pause briefly, then return without bouncing or letting the knees lift into the pad.

hypertrophy.rationale: Strong direct soleus stimulus with low unrelated fatigue, but seated knee flexion makes it less complete for gastrocnemius growth than a knee-extended calf raise.

strength.rationale: Loads plantar-flexion force directly, but the single-joint seated setup has limited carryover to whole-body strength expression.

joint_resilience.rationale: Provides controlled ankle and Achilles tendon exposure through useful range, with less knee-extended gastrocnemius length than standing options.

athletic_transfer.rationale: The ankle action is relevant to gait and jumping, but the seated supported setup removes posture, ground reaction, and coordination demands.

control.rationale: Very low Motor Control demand beyond ankle range, tempo, and keeping the knees settled under the pad.

fatigue_efficiency.rationale: High local calf stimulus with very low systemic fatigue, balance cost, or unrelated recovery demand.

setup.rationale: Requires a specific machine plus pad height and load setup, but the setup is quick and repeatable once adjusted.

ease.rationale: Simple guided movement with minimal skill demand; the main technique constraints are full range, controlled tempo, and pad placement.

progression.rationale: Load, reps, pauses, and range are easy to track, with minor limitations from machine increments and individual machine geometry.

support.rationale: Very high external support from the seat, thigh pad, foot platform, and guided resistance path.

primary.name: Soleus
primary.evidenceShort: Bent-knee calf raises preferentially emphasize soleus.
primary.evidence: Bent-knee calf-raise evidence shows greater acute soleus swelling than straight-leg calf raises, and seated knee-flexed training produced soleus hypertrophy comparable to standing training while limiting gastrocnemius growth.

secondary.name: Gastrocnemius
secondary.evidenceShort: Still contributes to plantar flexion, but knee flexion reduces its emphasis.
secondary.evidence: The gastrocnemius is part of the triceps surae and contributes during calf-raise tasks, but seated knee-flexed training produced much smaller or nonsignificant gastrocnemius hypertrophy than standing knee-extended training.

evidence.verdict: Seated machine calf raise: soleus primary; gastrocnemius secondary; no separate support muscles listed.
evidence.clinicalShort: Acute swelling, EMG, and MRI hypertrophy answer different questions and do not directly determine tendon tolerance or long-term programming by themselves.
evidence.limitsShort: Knee angle, foot platform height, dorsiflexion depth, pause duration, machine cam path, load, and bouncing change the training stress.
evidence.summary: The seated machine calf raise is classified as a supported bent-knee plantar-flexion exercise. Direct straight-leg versus bent-leg calf-raise evidence supports a soleus-biased classification, while gastrocnemius remains a secondary plantar-flexion contributor because knee flexion shortens the gastrocnemius and reduces its growth response relative to standing calf raises.
evidence.clinicalInterpretation: Ultrasound swelling and EMG studies estimate acute local use under specific exercise conditions, while MRI hypertrophy studies reflect training adaptation across weeks. These measures should be interpreted with knee angle, ankle range of motion, and loading method rather than treated as universal muscle-growth rankings.
evidence.limitations: This entry assumes a conventional seated calf-raise machine with the knees flexed near 90 degrees. Straight-knee standing, donkey, leg-press calf-raise, single-leg, and bodyweight variants should be classified separately because gastrocnemius and soleus emphasis changes with knee angle and setup.

studies.type: Straight-leg versus bent-leg calf-raise swelling study
studies.finding: Bent-leg calf raises produced greater soleus swelling, while straight-leg calf raises produced greater gastrocnemius swelling.
studies.citation: Kassiano W, Costa B, Kunevaliki G, Soares D, Stavinski N, Francsuel J, Carneiro MAS, Tricoli I, Nunes JP, Ribeiro AS, Cyrino ES. Muscle Swelling of the Triceps Surae in Response to Straight-Leg and Bent-Leg Calf Raise Exercises in Young Women. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research. 2023;37(7):e438-e443. doi:10.1519/JSC.0000000000004491.
studies.relevance: Direct knee-angle calf-raise comparison measuring medial gastrocnemius, lateral gastrocnemius, and soleus thickness before and after exercise.

studies.type: Standing versus seated calf-raise hypertrophy study
studies.finding: Seated knee-flexed calf-raise training increased soleus volume similarly to standing training but did not significantly increase gastrocnemius volume.
studies.citation: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, Eihara Y, Ono M, Sato M, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H. Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training. Frontiers in Physiology. 2023;14:1272106. doi:10.3389/fphys.2023.1272106.
studies.relevance: Direct seated versus standing calf-raise training comparison using MRI muscle volume outcomes for soleus and gastrocnemius heads.

studies.finding: Functional MRI and EMG characterized distinct gastrocnemius and soleus involvement in triceps-surae activation.
studies.citation: Kinugasa R, Akima H. Neuromuscular activation of triceps surae using muscle functional MRI and EMG. Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise. 2005;37(4):593-598. doi:10.1249/01.mss.0000159026.99792.76.
studies.relevance: Supports separating soleus and gastrocnemius rather than using one generic calf label.
